chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said on the authority of Ali ibn Abu al-Qasim, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ishaq that I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) asking him: How does the servant worship his Lord while he cannot see Him?

He (peace be upon him) replied in writing: O Abu Yusuf! My Master, my Lord, and the Benefactor upon me and my forefathers, is far above being seen. He said: I also asked whether the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw his Lord? He wrote back: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, manifested to the Messenger what He desired from the Light of His Magnitude.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad (AS), referring to Imam al-Hasan al-Askari
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَة: Vision (specifically in the context of seeing God)

ai.seo_question: Did Prophet Muhammad see God with his eyes or his heart?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tawhid elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'vision of the heart' (ru'ya al-qalb) versus 'physical vision' (ru'ya al-'ayn), resolving the apparent contradiction in how believers worship an unseen God. The Imam distinguishes between the Prophet Muhammad’s unique spiritual perception of Divine light through his heart and the general limitation of physical eyes, affirming that true worship relies on this inner certainty rather than visual manifestation.
